items.title: Deutsche Bank, PNB ink pact to fund M&As
items.description: Deutsche Bank and Punjab National Bank have signed a preliminary agreement to finance corporate acquisitions in India. This partnership follows recent reforms that allow domestic lenders to fund up to 75% of corporate deal values. State Bank of India has also entered a similar partnership with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group. The agreement aims to support Indian companies in their growth and strategic expansion efforts.

items.title: These mid-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of over 25%, according to analysts
items.description: There is a new worry for the market, and it is best to be prepared for it. After almost six months, the threat of US tariffs is back. Tariff talk is exactly the kind of thing that impacts sentiment without touching the fundamentals of companies.

items.title: India's net FDI outflows widen to $4.95 billion in September
items.description: India's foreign direct investment landscape saw a net outflow of $4.95 billion in September, markedly higher than last year. In the same month, gross inflows decreased by 17.6%, totaling $5.91 billion, impacted by a rise in repatriation and disinvestment. Indian firms invested $4.41 billion abroad. Yet, from April to September, net FDI inflows surged, with total gross inflows up by 15.5% to $60.91 billion.

items.title: Gujarat overtakes Maharashtra as India's top state for active investors
items.description: Gujarat has become the state with the highest number of active investors, surpassing Maharashtra. The data indicates a significant increase in the number of active investors in recent months. Active investors in Maharashtra also increased, but not as much as in Gujarat. Additionally, Uttar Pradesh remains in third place, showing growth in its investor count. The total active unique investors in India reached a two-year high in October.

items.title: Indian stocks defy Asia rout, hit fresh FY27 highs on global fund rotation
items.description: India's equity indices saw a notable increase as they defied trends in the Asia-Pacific region. Investor confidence was bolstered by resilient domestic corporate earnings and decreased focus on AI stocks. Key contributors to this rise included ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and Reliance Industries. Meanwhile, foreign funds recorded significant investments in Indian equities, marking a shift in market dynamics. Overall, Indian markets remained comparatively stable despite fluctuating conditions in Asian markets.

items.title: D-Street poised for a positive start as GIFT Nifty trades firmly higher
items.description: Markets experienced a significant rebound, recovering nearly 2% from Monday's sell-off, indicating strong underlying buying interest. Analysts suggest that despite the recovery, some consolidation may be necessary in the near term. Foreign portfolio investors net bought shares worth Rs 4,479 crore, while domestic investors were net sellers at Rs 4,019 crore. The Indian rupee rose to its highest level this financial year due to strong foreign inflows.

items.title: Stocks in news: LG Electronics, HDFC Bank, Siemens Energy, Lupin and Schaeffler India
items.description: Domestic equities rebounded strongly as the Nifty 50 surged by 470 points post-market holiday. Major players like LG Electronics India and HDFC Bank made headlines with noteworthy updates, reigniting investor enthusiasm. Waaree Renewable Technologies received a favorable assessment from CARE Ratings, improving its financial outlook. Additionally, Siemens Energy showcased impressive quarterly earnings, reflecting strong growth in both revenue and profit margins.

items.title: Retail investors turn net sellers in November as FIIs pile into Indian stocks
items.description: In November, retail investors, mutual funds, and insurance companies sold significant amounts of Indian growth assets. Retail investors experienced their largest selling in history, totaling around ₹24,953 crore. This marks the second consecutive month of outflows from retail investors. Additionally, mutual funds reported their first monthly net selling since August 2022, amounting to ₹34,929 crore. Despite the selling trend, retail investors have maintained a net buying position in 2026.

items.title: Gold crash triggers auction notices as LTV breaches hit lenders
items.description: Gold finance companies are issuing legal auction notices due to breaches in loan-to-value limits amid falling gold prices. This trend has been driven by a significant decline in gold prices over the past weeks. Nearly 40% of gold-loan portfolios have seen their loan-to-value ratios exceed permissible levels. Lenders are encouraging borrowers to provide additional collateral or make partial payments to avoid auctions.

items.title: Govt mulls special shares to retain control of merged PFC-REC entity
items.description: In a strategic move, the Centre is planning a capital structure featuring special shares to facilitate the PFC-REC merger, ensuring majority voting control. To finance this initiative, the government is expected to allocate around Rs 7,500-8,000 crore despite holding a lower share post-merger. The plan will also include issuing shares with ordinary and enhanced voting rights, subject to Cabinet approval for the proposed funding.

items.title: Stock Radar: Union Bank of India stock hit a fresh record high in November 2026; time to buy or book profits?
items.description: Union Bank of India reached a fresh record high following a breakout from an inverse head and shoulders pattern. The stock has noted significant gains, increasing by over 19% in the last month alone. Trading volumes have surged, demonstrating strong buying participation from market participants. Traders are advised to maintain a positive outlook with a potential target of 255 to 290 levels.

items.title: PSBs may find it hard to keep lending pace as liquidity tightens
items.description: Public sector banks could struggle to sustain aggressive loan growth amid diminishing liquidity advantages and growing deposit challenges. The loan-to-deposit ratios of public and private sector banks have shown significant narrowing recently. Private sector banks' deposit growth outpaced that of public sector banks, impacting their competitive edge. State-owned banks have expressed optimism about liquidity positions while acknowledging potential pressure on deposit rates.

items.title: Inflation pressures broaden across India, raising rate-hike risks ahead of RBI's December review
items.description: Inflationary pressures spread across goods, services and regions in October, with a larger share of items breaching the 4% threshold, the RBI's November bulletin showed. Retail inflation climbed to 6.09%, crossing the central bank's upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years, potentially complicating its December monetary policy decision.

items.title: Noel Tata-led trust gets nod to invest Rs 150 crore in financially sound companies
items.description: Maharashtra charity commissioner has granted permission to Tata Social Welfare Trust for new investment opportunities. The trust can now invest ₹150 crore in shares of financially stable and well-governed companies. This expansion includes investments through a dedicated vehicle monitored by an investment committee. The trust plans to regularly assess investments while ensuring compliance with all necessary regulations. Qualified advisers will assist in overseeing investment decisions, enhancing the fund’s strategic management.

items.title: Indian investors clock $353 million in overseas gains; Nvidia, Micron among most-traded US stocks: Vested
items.description: In November 2026, Indian investors celebrated remarkable gains totaling $353 million from both realized and unrealized overseas investments. A notable 40% of this success stemmed from artificial intelligence stocks on Vested. Active investors on the platform surged by 51% when compared to the previous year. Furthermore, non-resident Indian investors showcased much larger average portfolios, signaling a robust trend in global investment participation within the Indian investor community.

items.title: Inflation scare? Rising prices could squeeze India Inc profits in Q3, says Icra
items.description: Indian companies could see revenue growth moderate to 18-20% in Q3 FY27, while operating profit margins may decline 50-75 basis points year-on-year, ICRA estimates. Rising raw material, energy and logistics costs, higher borrowing rates and weakening rural demand could weigh on profitability, even as domestic-focused sectors remain relatively resilient.

items.title: Tata Steel shares recover over 2% after sliding 10% in 2 days. What should investors do?
items.description: Tata Steel shares rebound after two sessions of sharp losses following its proposed APL Apollo deal. Brokerages retain Buy ratings, citing downstream expansion and potential valuation benefits, while execution risks and acquisition funding remain key concerns.

items.title: Sebi appoints forensic auditor to probe alleged Rs 3,535 crore fund diversion at Coffee Day Enterprises
items.description: Sebi has appointed CLA Indus Value Consulting as forensic auditor to assist in a fresh investigation into Coffee Day Enterprises over the alleged diversion of Rs 3,535 crore from seven subsidiaries to a promoter-linked entity. The appointment follows a November 5 SAT order setting aside Sebi's earlier ruling and directing an independent probe to be completed within six months.

items.title: $100 billion FII inflow possible? JPMorgan gives 29,000 target for Nifty
items.description: JPMorgan has set a Nifty target of 29,000 by end-2027, citing improving corporate earnings, easing oil prices and resilient domestic demand. The brokerage sees potential for $100 billion in foreign equity inflows if global long-only funds restore their India exposure to benchmark weights, but flags valuation and policy risks.

items.title: Coca Cola bottler gears up for India IPO to rival Pepsi’s Varun Beverages. How do they stack up?
items.description: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings is preparing for an IPO, backed by strong brand leadership, a 1.7-million-outlet distribution network and India's growing beverage market. Improving profitability, positive free cash flow and a net cash position strengthen its outlook, while comparisons with Varun Beverages highlight competitive challenges and growth opportunities.

items.title: India’s MTF book jumps 5-fold to Rs 1.5 lakh crore as F&O curbs drive retail shift to cash markets
items.description: India's MTF book has grown more than five-fold to Rs 1.5 lakh crore since April 2022, driven by F&O curbs, retail participation and brokers' revenue diversification. Smallcap stocks account for over half the book, raising liquidity and forced-selling risks, while MTF creates an additional income stream for brokers and exchanges.

items.title: Sugar stocks rally up to 15% as ISMA projects drop in 2026-27 output; Dhampur Sugar, Uttam Sugar lead gains
items.description: Sugar stocks surged up to 15% after ISMA projected India’s 2026-27 net sugar output would fall to 265.21 lakh tonnes from 279.71 lakh tonnes a year earlier. Lower cane acreage, uneven monsoon rainfall and weaker output in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh could tighten supplies and support domestic sugar prices.

items.title: Rupee rebound is bad news for IT stocks. Jefferies sees rerating potential only for Infosys, Sagility
items.description: The rupee’s sharp appreciation is putting Indian IT companies under pressure, threatening earnings and operating margins amid sluggish growth and pricing challenges. A 1% rise in the rupee could cut FY28 earnings per share by 2-5%, depending on the company. Jefferies sees limited rerating potential across the sector, favouring Infosys among largecaps and Sagility among midcaps.

items.title: NSE becomes world's 3rd largest listed exchange, overtakes London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Boerse AG
items.description: NSE has become the world’s third-largest listed stock exchange operator with a market capitalisation of $64 billion, overtaking Germany’s Deutsche Boerse AG ($63 billion) and the UK’s London Stock Exchange ($62 billion).

items.title: US tariff issue comes back to haunt investors. Which stocks and sectors can get impacted?
items.description: A proposed US tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods has put export-linked stocks in focus, with chemicals, textiles and capital goods facing potential exposure. Navin Fluorine, PI Industries, SRF, Welspun Living and Cummins India are among the stocks to watch.

items.title: Why did market rise today? Sensex ends 390 pts higher, Nifty above 25,850. 5 factors behind Rs 3 lakh crore gain
items.description: Nifty and Sensex experienced gains as banking, IT, and metal stocks rallied significantly in the market. The total market capitalization of BSE rose by Rs 1.56 lakh crore to Rs 514 lakh crore. Foreign institutional investors are showing strong interest in Indian stocks amid the decreasing appeal of AI-linked equities. Key stocks like HDFC Bank and Reliance Industries have seen notable increases in their share prices.

items.title: Siemens Energy shares rally 6% on strong Q4 earnings, dividend announcement
items.description: Siemens Energy India shares rose on Thursday after the company reported an 82% YoY jump in Q4 FY26 net profit to Rs 653 crore. Revenue increased 30.5% to Rs 3,453 crore, while EBITDA surged 72% to Rs 822 crore.

items.title: Rs 1.70 lakh crore gain! TCS, Infosys, other IT stocks rally up to 11% in just 4 days. What’s fuelling the surge?
items.description: IT stocks have rallied up to 11% in four sessions, adding Rs 1.70 lakh crore to their combined market capitalisation. However, brokerages remain cautious about a broad-based recovery, citing weak deal conversion, AI-led disruption and margin pressures.

items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields to list on Nov 27: How Coal India's subsidiaries BCCL, CMPDI fared on D-Street
items.description: Mahanadi Coalfields will be listed on November 27, attracting investor attention due to previous IPO outcomes. Both Bharat Coking Coal and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute had varied listing experiences earlier this year. While BCCL debuted strongly with significant demand, CMPDI faced subdued investor interest upon listing. MCL's IPO, significantly larger than its predecessors, demonstrated strong demand from institutional investors.

items.title: US tariffs on India: What a proposed 25% Trump levy means for exports, GDP growth and stocks
items.description: India’s export outlook faces fresh uncertainty as the US proposes tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, potentially putting exporters at a disadvantage against Asian peers. While a trade deal could lower the rate to 17%, sectors such as textiles, chemicals and capital goods remain exposed. Analysts, however, expect limited near-term market impact, with export diversification offering some cushion.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A top IT firm for a 6.85% gain, a large-cap capital goods maker stock for a 7% upmove
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
items.description: Indian stock markets extended their winning streak for a second session on Thursday, with the Sensex rising 400 points and the Nifty nearing 26,000, led by IT, banking and metal stocks. Investors will track global cues, foreign fund flows, crude oil prices and key stock-specific developments for Friday's trading session.

items.title: Market Trading Guide: Tech Mahindra, Angel One among 5 stock recommendations for Friday
items.description: Indian equities recovered from early losses in a volatile session, as sustained foreign inflows and selective buying outweighed firm crude and the proposed US tariffs. Analysts say near-term sentiment remains constructive but volatile, as foreign liquidity should help limit the downside, while global rates, crude and trade negotiations could cap valuation expansion.Here are five stock recommendations for Friday

items.title: BSE Index Services gets Sebj registration to operate as index provider
items.description: BSE Index Services has received Sebi registration to operate as an index provider under the regulator's Index Providers Regulations, 2024. Effective November 25, the approval follows RBI authorisation allowing it to administer non-significant benchmarks, strengthening its position in the index administration business.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: For investors with a 1- to 2-year view, who can ignore volatility: 6 large-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 24%
items.description: The right response to a sudden spurt in volatility is not to turn bearish; neither is it to drop your guard. It is the stance that has remained valid these past weeks: Cautiously optimistic, but with the caution pointed at one thing in particular, which is what you buy. When oil is a live risk, extra care over where fresh money goes is not optional.

items.title: NSE among 6 stocks hitting 52-week highs; stock rallies up to 35% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex climbed 390 points to settle at 84,328 on Thursday. Riding the market rally, six stocks from the BSE 100 index hit fresh 52-week highs, touching their highest price levels in the past 12 months. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the last year and may indicate heightened market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Market wrap: HCL Tech, BSE, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian stock markets ended higher on Thursday, with the Sensex rising 390 points and the Nifty gaining 65 points. IT and capital markets stocks led the rally, while banking, FMCG and auto shares faced selling pressure. HCL Tech and BSE topped the gainers, while Asian Paints and Bajaj Finance led the losers.

items.title: Patanjali Foods declares second interim dividend of Rs 1.25 per share; sets Dec 11 as record date
items.description: Patanjali Foods declared a second interim dividend of ₹1.25 per share for FY27, setting December 11 as the record date and payment due by December 25. This announcement follows the company's report of lower second-quarter profit despite higher revenue, while its shares have declined nearly 27% so far this year.
